reference.title: Dumbbell External Rotation
reference.listing: Page not read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the forearm rotates up, breathe in as it lowers.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s up, short pause, about 2.5 s down

prescription.effort: Stop 2-3 reps short of failure (RIR 2-3); no pain
prescription.progression: Add reps, then a slightly heavier dumbbell

cues.text: Lie on your left side, knees bent, head resting on the left arm. Right elbow bent 90 degrees and tucked against the side, forearm across the belly, dumbbell near the floor.
Breathe out and turn the forearm up like a door on a hinge; the elbow stays pinned to the side.
Forearm points up toward the ceiling (or as far as is comfortable); shoulder blade back.
Breathe in and lower slowly back across the belly.
Brief pause; repeat. Then switch sides.

mistakes.mistake: Elbow lifting away from the side
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow pinned to the ribs (a folded towel between arm and side helps).

mistakes.mistake: Rolling the trunk back to lift the weight
mistakes.fix: Stay stacked on your side; only the forearm moves.
Use a very light weight; this is a small muscle.

kinematics.norm: From the forearm across the belly to pointing up (about 90-100 degrees of rotation); side-lying external rotation gave the highest infraspinatus (62% MVIC) and teres minor (67% MVIC) activity of the ER exercises tested (Reinold 2004)
Elbow bent 90 degrees, upper arm along the side (clinical opinion)
Side-lying, knees bent, head supported (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #11216, Dumbbell External Rotation, video (movement reference only; page not read)

Reinold, Wilk, Fleisig, Zheng, Barrentine, Chmielewski, Cody, Jameson and Andrews 2004, electromyographic analysis of the rotator cuff and deltoid musculature during common shoulder external rotation exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 34(7):385-394)

Andersen, Andersen, Mortensen, Poulsen, Bjornlund and Zebis 2010, muscle activation and perceived loading during rehabilitation exercises: comparison of dumbbells and elastic resistance (Phys Ther 90(4):538-549)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Rotator cuff work: use a light dumbbell and a slow, pain-free range.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: smaller range, towel roll between the elbow and the side.
Bottom shoulder uncomfortable: put a pillow under the head.

muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Prime mover (with teres minor): external rotation; highest of the ER exercises in side-lying (Reinold 2004).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Keep the shoulder blade set back.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Light: keeps the elbow at the side.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Keep the trunk stacked on its side.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Keep the trunk stacked on its side.

guides.label: Forearm turns up about the elbow
